additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise) aimed at preventing weight gain. Core psychological features include an overvaluation of weight and shape, intense fear of weight gain, and a sense of loss of control during binges, with self-worth heavily tied to body image. The disorder typically has an onset in adolescence or young adulthood and often follows periods of dieting, weight-related criticism, or stressful life transitions; it can occur at normal, above, or below-average body weight, which helps distinguish it from anorexia nervosa. The course can be chronic or intermittent, and medical complications may arise from purging and nutritional instability, even when overall functioning appears relatively intact in work or school settings.

patient.personality: Oscar is laid-back, creative, and socially engaged, blending mechanical skill with artistic and community-focused interests.
patient.stressor: Oscar moved out of his family home around five months ago to share an apartment with coworkers so he could be closer to the warehouse and save for his long-term goals, abruptly shifting from a structured family environment with shared meals to an irregular schedule built around rotating shifts and social outings. Without his mother’s home cooking and family routines, he began skipping meals during long shifts and then spending late nights hanging out with friends, ordering large amounts of takeout after games, open mics, or concerts. At the same time, he became more self-conscious about his body as he compared himself to athletic friends and online images, experimenting with strict food rules during the day and then feeling like he was undoing everything at night. Over several months, this unstable pattern around food and body image became distressing enough that he confided in a mentor at the community garden, who encouraged him to see a psychiatrist when he admitted he was regularly eating way more than he intended and then trying extreme measures afterward to make up for it.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep ending up eating way more than I meant to in one sitting, like way more than anyone else around me.”

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Ever since I moved in with the guys, I freak out about gaining even a couple pounds, like if I eat one slice of pizza more than them I picture my stomach blowing up and feel like I’ve ruined everything for the week.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: My whole mood and how I feel about myself that day is based on whether I think I look lean in the mirror before work or if my gut sticks out in my coveralls, and if I think I look bigger I just feel like a loser no matter what else I get done.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: After those late-night takeout binges, I usually end up in the bathroom making myself throw up and telling myself it’s just to ‘fix’ the damage so I don’t get fat.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On nights after a long shift, I’ll order a big burger meal and then still go through almost a whole large pizza and chips by myself while we’re watching a game, way past the point where everyone else has stopped eating.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it’s like a switch flips and I just keep shoveling food in even while I’m thinking, ‘dude, stop, you don’t even want this,’ but my hands just keep going until everything’s gone and I feel sick.
